system:
You draft the work brief for an illustration engine: one page that tells every illustrator how this whole work looks and feels. You get the work's title and author, the draft briefs the reading pass wrote for each of its divisions, and the ordered list of the work's story sections (id, division, title).

Return:
1. tone: one line on the mood every picture of this work should carry.
2. depiction_rules: a short list of how certain things in the work may or may not be shown, drawn from the divisions' drafts, the text and what you know about the work. Each rule is one line.
3. eras: one or more stretches of the work's world. Each has a short name and four lines: people (who lives in it and what they look like), dress, buildings and objects, and technology (what exists and what does not yet exist). Use as few eras as the work needs: one when the whole work shares a setting, several when its people, dress or technology change from one stretch of the story to the next.
4. assignments: every story section belongs to exactly one era. Give runs of consecutive sections in the order listed: each run names its first and last section id and its era. The runs must cover every section in order, with no gaps and no overlaps.

The brief holds only what is true for the whole work or a whole era. One person or place is described in the cast, not here. One episode's look belongs to its section, not here. Do not write rules or era lines about a single character, place or episode.

Keep the tone, rules and eras under 400 words in total.

parsed.tone: Reverent and awe-struck, with grounded human intimacy in household and village scenes, dread and holiness in signs of God's presence, grief and suspense in conflict, and quiet luminous hope at the close.
depiction_rules: Depict God only through signs such as the burning bush, pillar of cloud and fire, glory, light, thunder or wind; never as a visible human-like form, and do not depict God the Father in human form.
Show the Holy Spirit as a dove or as wind or breath only where the text names it.
Angels and the divine voice appear as light, cloud and posture rather than detailed flesh where possible.
Show plagues, sea and the suffering of Egypt plainly as natural catastrophe, without gratuitous gore.
Handle violence, including the crucifixion, the golden calf and the slaying of idolaters, with gravity and restraint.
Satan and demons are shown as dark or distorted presences, not detailed monsters.
Depict Jesus as a 1st-century Jewish man, without the halo-and-blue-robe stereotype unless a scene calls for a glory motif.
Avoid caricaturing Jews, Pharisees, Samaritans, Judas or Gentiles; opponents and crowds keep individual dignity.
Women appear throughout as full participants, not as background or as mother-and-child emphasis beyond the text.
Sanctuary furnishings follow the given pattern in gold, acacia wood, bronze and blue, purple and scarlet linen.
Sombre understatement for the deaths of Saul and his sons; no gore in battle scenes.

eras.name: Late Bronze Age Egypt and Sinai wilderness
eras.people: Egyptians of the New Kingdom with shaved heads and linen kilts, Hebrew families as desert-dwelling laborers, Midianite herders.
eras.dress: Linen kilts and wigs for Egyptians, simple tunics and cloaks for Israelites; tabernacle priests in linen tunic, robe, ephod, breastplate and turban.
eras.buildings_and_objects: Brick storage cities, Egyptian palaces and chariots, goatskin tents, portable tabernacle with acacia boards, gold overlay and bronze altar.
eras.technology: Chariots, bronze and gold working, woven linen and goat-hair cloth, mud brick, papyrus boats; no iron in common use, writing only as inscriptions and engraved stones.

eras.name: Iron Age Canaan and Israelite hill country, c. 11th century BCE
eras.people: Israelites in tribal villages and hill towns, Philistines in coastal cities, Ammonites, Moabites and Amalekites to east and south; shepherds with staffs.
eras.dress: Simple wool or linen tunics, cloaks and sashes; women in long dresses and veils; kings and warriors in bronze helmets and mail; Philistines in heavy bronze armor.
eras.buildings_and_objects: Mud-brick and stone houses, walled towns, tents and high places, tabernacle with ark, bronze and iron weapons, slings, clay pottery, oxcarts.
eras.technology: Iron tools and weapons, chariots and horses, oxcarts, lamps and grain storage; no coined money and writing only as simple records.

eras.name: First-century Roman Judea and Galilee, c. AD 30
eras.people: Jewish villagers, farmers, fishermen, shepherds, tax collectors, priests, Pharisees, Sadducees, Roman soldiers and officials, Samaritans; Eastern Mediterranean people with olive or brown skin.
eras.dress: Linen and wool tunics, mantles, head coverings and veils, tassels for devout men; priests in white linen; Roman soldiers in armor; wealthy in purple and fine linen.
eras.buildings_and_objects: Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs, village wells, Herodian temple, synagogues, rock-cut tombs with rolling stones, oil lamps, boats and nets, vineyards, scrolls.
eras.technology: Oil lamps, hand-milled grain, looms, plows, Roman roads and denarii; scrolls and wax tablets; no printing, clocks, firearms or machinery.
